mutations.name: a-leftover-loses-its-line-number
mutations._mechanism: A hit without a line number is the manual re-grep the sweep exists to replace.

mutations.name: the-allowlist-is-ignored
mutations._mechanism: Every deliberate explanation becomes a leftover, so the report is noise and the reader stops reading it.

mutations.name: an-allowed-hit-is-dropped-silently
mutations._mechanism: The allowlist becomes a place real leftovers can hide, because nothing prints what it swallowed.

mutations.name: history-is-treated-as-a-leftover
mutations._mechanism: Handoffs and archives are records of sessions that already happened; flagging them buries the hits a reader can act on. Measured 5 of 26 on the first live run.

mutations.name: history-is-dropped-instead-of-counted
mutations._mechanism: A silent skip and an empty tree print the same thing — the failure mode every suppression in this repo is written to avoid.

mutations.name: include-history-does-nothing
mutations._mechanism: The escape hatch is advertised and inert, so a reader who needs the historical hits cannot get them.

mutations.name: machine-logs-are-searched
mutations._mechanism: `.bkit`/`.omc` are append-only tool state; on the first live run they were 14 of 26 hits and outnumbered everything actionable.

mutations.name: the-excerpt-is-truncated-from-the-left
mutations._mechanism: On a long line the printed excerpt does not contain the identifier being swept for — the one thing an excerpt owes its reader. Measured on a 900-character JSON log line.

mutations.name: stem-hits-are-folded-into-leftovers
mutations._mechanism: Prose naming the concept after a renamed file floods the verdict, which is the sweep's main source of noise.

mutations.name: an-empty-stem-matches-every-line
mutations._mechanism: `"" in line` is always true, so an extensionless identifier turns every non-matching line in the tree into a `related:` hit. Replaces an earlier mutation (`_stem_of` returning the identifier itself) that was an EQUIVALENT MUTANT: with stem == identifier the `elif` branch is unreachable, so the behaviour was byte-identical and its survival measured nothing.
mutations.find: elif stems[identifier] and stems[identifier] in line:
mutations.replace: elif stems[identifier] is not None and stems[identifier] in line:

mutations.name: a-binary-file-aborts-the-sweep
mutations._mechanism: One undecodable blob would discard every real finding in the same run.

mutations.name: mutation-anchors-lose-their-surface
mutations._mechanism: The surface the row calls the one most often missed stops being visible in the report.

mutations.name: an-empty-identifier-is-accepted
mutations._mechanism: An empty needle matches every line of every file: a sweep that reports everything is as useful as one that reports nothing, and looks far more thorough.

mutations.name: an-unreadable-root-reads-as-clean
mutations._mechanism: Nothing was searched, so CLEAN would be a cannot-judge wearing a verdict — the exact confusion every other h-mad gate is written to prevent.

mutations.name: the-cli-exits-0-on-leftovers
mutations._mechanism: A caller reading `$?` cannot distinguish a clean sweep from a dirty one — and the token exists precisely because `$?` is the wrong surface.

mutations.name: the-judgement-disclaimer-is-dropped
mutations._mechanism: Without it `LEFTOVERS` reads as a verdict that the hits are wrong, and a reader trained by that deletes correct prose.
